title: ‘Disaster’ unfolding as Sydney fire ant outbreak partly blamed on ignored biosecurity recommendations
paragraphs: Years-old recommendations by Australia’s biosecurity watchdog have been ignored or not acted on by successive federal governments, increasing the risk of an invasive pest outbreak such as the fire ants discovered in Sydney this week, according to experts.

Environmentalists and biosecurity experts warn the large colony of red imported fire ants is a warning sign that the country’s quarantine system is too slow-moving, underfunded and overly concerned with agriculture.
The nest was found in Auburn and is the second outbreak of the invasive species in Sydney this year after they were discovered at the Enfield intermodal logistics centre on 23 September.
